sso.passwordLoginDisabledDesc: Users must sign in via SSO

sso.name: Provider name

sso.provisioningDisabled: Disabled — existing linked identities can still log in, but no new links

sso.requireEmailVerifiedDesc: Disable for self-hosted providers (PocketID, Kanidm, etc.) that do not issue email_verified: true in their tokens.

sso.rpLogoutDesc: On sign-out, also end the session at this provider by redirecting to its end-session endpoint, not just clearing MailExpert’s cookie. Requires the provider to advertise an end_session_endpoint and to have your MailExpert login URL (…/login) registered as a post-logout redirect URI.
sso.adminGroupClaimDesc: JWT claim name that contains the user's groups (e.g. groups). Leave blank to disable group-based admin assignment.
sso.adminGroupValueDesc: The group name that grants admin access. Users in this group become admins on every SSO login; users not in this group lose admin access.
sso.loginMatchClaimDesc: OIDC claim matched against each MailExpert account’s username when an SSO login is first linked to an existing account (provisioning mode “login existing only”). Defaults to email. Use preferred_username, upn, etc. for identity providers where usernames are not email addresses — only if your provider guarantees the claim is unique and not user-editable.
sso.deleteConfirmBody: All linked user identities for this provider will also be removed. Users with no other login method will be locked out.
sso.errorRequired: Name, slug, issuer URL and client ID are required.

integrations.title: Integrations

microsoft.title: Microsoft 365 / Outlook.com
microsoft.description: OAuth2 for work, school, or personal Microsoft accounts (Outlook.com, Hotmail)
microsoft.step1: Go to portal.azure.com → Microsoft Entra ID → App registrations → New registration. Under Supported account types, select 'Accounts in any organizational directory and personal Microsoft accounts' to allow Outlook.com/Hotmail logins
microsoft.step2: Set redirect URI type to Web and paste the URI shown below
microsoft.step3: API permissions → Add a permission → APIs my organization uses (search 'Exchange' if not listed) → Office 365 Exchange Online → Delegated → IMAP.AccessAsUser.All and SMTP.Send
microsoft.step4: API permissions → Add a permission → Microsoft Graph → Delegated → offline_access, openid, email, profile
microsoft.step5: Click Grant admin consent for your organization (org/work accounts only — personal accounts skip this step)
microsoft.step6: Certificates & secrets → New client secret — copy the Value (not the ID)
microsoft.tenantIdNote: Use 'consumers' for personal Outlook.com/Hotmail only, 'common' for both personal and org, or your tenant UUID for a single organization
microsoft.redirectUriNote: This must exactly match the redirect URI registered in Azure. Suggested: {{uri}}
microsoft.savedNote: Configuration saved. Click "Connect account" to authorize.
microsoft.connectedNote: Microsoft 365 account connected successfully! Check the Accounts tab.

googleApps.title: Google apps
googleApps.description: OAuth apps that Gmail mailboxes connect through. An unverified Google Cloud project accepts at most 100 users over its lifetime, so MailExpert spreads mailboxes across several apps.
googleApps.callbackNote: The same for every app. Register it in each app's OAuth client.
googleApps.callbackNotSaved: Not saved yet: this is the address of the page you are on. Save it before adding apps.
googleApps.callbackOtherHost: You opened the panel through another address. If people connect Gmail from here, also register: {{uri}}
googleApps.step1: Create a separate Google Cloud project for each app: OAuth clients of one project share its 100-user limit.
googleApps.step2: On the OAuth consent screen choose the External audience and publish the app (In Production). Do not use Testing: access there expires after 7 days.
googleApps.step4: Credentials → Create credentials → OAuth client ID → Web application; add the callback URL above to Authorized redirect URIs.
googleApps.step5: Add the app below with its client ID and client secret.
googleApps.empty: No apps yet. Gmail cannot be connected until one is added.
googleApps.importDropHint: Or drag and drop the client JSON file downloaded from Google Cloud Console here.
googleApps.importClear: Enter client ID and secret manually instead
googleApps.clientIdFixed: The client ID of an app does not change. Another client ID is another app.
googleApps.clientSecretKeep: Leave empty to keep the stored secret.
googleApps.userLimitHint: Lower it if the project had users before MailExpert: Google counts them too.
googleApps.disableConfirm: Mailboxes that will need a reconnect: {{count}}. They reconnect through another app.
googleApps.deleteConfirm: The record of addresses this app has served is deleted with it.
googleApps.deleteInUse: An app can be deleted once no mailbox uses it.
googleApps.errorGeneric: The request failed. Please try again.
googleApps.errorLabelInvalid: Enter a name of 1 to 100 characters.
googleApps.errorClientIdInvalid: This is not a Google OAuth client ID. It ends with .apps.googleusercontent.com.
googleApps.errorClientSecretRedacted: The client secret contains a hidden-value character. Paste the full secret.
googleApps.errorUserLimitInvalid: The user limit must be a positive whole number.
googleApps.errorAppExists: This client ID is already added.
googleApps.errorSameProject: An app from this Google Cloud project is already added. Clients of one project share its limit.
googleApps.errorInUse: The app still has connected mailboxes.
googleApps.errorNotFound: The app no longer exists. Reload the page.
googleApps.errorCallbackInvalid: Enter a full address starting with https:// or http://.
googleApps.errorClientJsonInvalid: This is not valid JSON, or not a Google OAuth client file.
googleApps.errorClientJsonServiceAccount: This is a service account key, not an OAuth client. Download the OAuth client JSON instead (Credentials -> OAuth client -> Download JSON).
googleApps.errorClientJsonNotWeb: This is a desktop (installed) OAuth client. Create a Web application client instead.
googleApps.errorClientJsonIncomplete: The file is missing a client ID or client secret.
googleApps.errorClientJsonConflict: Provide either the client JSON file or a client ID and secret, not both.
googleApps.warningRedirectUriMissing: The file's redirect URIs do not include the panel's callback URL. Add it in Google Cloud Console: {{uri}}
googleApps.warningCallbackNotConfigured: No callback URL is saved yet. Save it above, then check this app's redirect URIs in Google Cloud Console.
googleApps.gmailApiDisabledWarning: Gmail API is off in this Google Cloud project: mail goes through SMTP. Enable Gmail API in the project.

accessSync.title: Cloudflare Access policy sync
accessSync.description: MailExpert keeps the Allow policy of the Cloudflare Access application in line with approved users: user changes reach the policy within seconds, and the whole list is checked every hour. Emails added in Cloudflare by hand, groups and domain rules stay as they are. A user whose email is removed in Cloudflare is disabled here.
accessSync.enabled: Sync approved users to the policy
accessSync.apiTokenHint: Needs the "Access: Apps and Policies" write permission for this account only. The token is stored encrypted and never shown.
accessSync.apiTokenStored: A token is stored. Enter a new one to replace it.
accessSync.limit: A run stops instead of disabling more than {{max}} users or more than half of the active users.
accessSync.outcomeUpdated: Policy updated: {{added}} added, {{removed}} removed, {{disabled}} users disabled.
accessSync.outcomeUnchanged: Policy was already up to date; {{disabled}} users disabled.
accessSync.outcomeAborted: Stopped: {{wouldDisable}} users would have been disabled. Nothing was changed; see the audit log.
accessSync.outcomeEmpty: Skipped: the policy would have no rules left.
accessSync.errorTokenUnreadable: the stored token cannot be decrypted, enter it again
accessSync.errorPolicyNotAllow: the policy is not an Allow policy
accessSync.errorNotAttached: the policy is not attached to this application
accessSync.errorInternal: internal error, see the server log
accessSync.errorInvalidId: The account ID is 32 hexadecimal characters; the application and policy IDs are UUIDs.
accessSync.errorIncomplete: To turn the sync on, fill in every ID and the API token.
accessSync.notConfigured: The sync is off or not filled in.
accessSync.notGoogleMode: The sync works only with AUTH_MODE=google.
accessSync.loadFailed: Could not load the sync settings: {{message}}

mailNode.title: Mail node
mailNode.description: The mailcow server where MailExpert creates mailboxes on your domains. Deleting such a mailbox is scheduled: it keeps working for the days set below, then MailExpert deletes it on the node for good, with its mail.
mailNode.hostNote: A host name, never an IP: mailboxes connect to it by IMAP and SMTP and the API is at https://<host>/api/v1, so moving the node is a DNS change.
mailNode.apiKeyNote: A read-write key from the mailcow admin page, allowed only from the address of this panel.
mailNode.quotaLabel: Quota of a new mailbox, MB
mailNode.quotaNote: A quota only caps a mailbox and reserves no disk. Up to {{max}} MB per mailbox.
mailNode.pingNote: Every 10 minutes the panel reads the mail disk and pings this URL: success below 85%, /fail above. A monitoring service with alerts (for example to Telegram) also warns when pings stop.
mailNode.saved: Saved: the mail node accepted the key.
mailNode.diskWarn: Free up space or grow the disk.
mailNode.newDomainNote: The panel sets the domain's relayhost, DKIM key and send limits on the node by itself. DNS records and the Microsoft EOP connectors are set up by hand (see the mail node runbook) and confirmed step by step in the domain details. Mailboxes can be created once the domain is ready.
mailNode.errorNotConfigured: The mail node is not set up.
mailNode.errorUnreachable: The mail node does not answer: check the host name, HTTPS and the firewall.
mailNode.errorAuth: The mail node refused the API key, or the address of this panel may not use the API.
mailNode.errorRefused: The mail node refused the request.
mailNode.errorHost: Enter a host name such as mail.example.com.
mailNode.errorQuota: The quota must be a whole number of MB from 1 to 102400.
mailNode.errorPingUrl: The ping URL must start with https://.
mailNode.errorDomain: Enter a domain name such as example.com.
mailNode.errorMailboxes: The mailbox limit must be a whole number from 1 to 10000.
mailNode.stepNodeConfigured: The node is set up for the domain: relayhost to the EOP host, DKIM, send limits (see the node settings of the domain below).
mailNode.stepDnsOk: DNS is published: MX to EOP, SPF, DKIM, DMARC and the tenant verification record.
mailNode.stepTenantVerified: The domain is added to the Microsoft tenant and verified.
mailNode.stepInternalRelay: The domain is an Internal Relay accepted domain in the tenant.
mailNode.stepConnectorReady: The Outbound connector lists the domain and delivers it to the node.
mailNode.stepReady: A test letter went both ways through EOP: mailboxes can be created.
mailNode.originAdopted: Made on the node by hand, adopted by {{by}}, {{at}}.
mailNode.originExistingMailboxes: Taken in as ready at the upgrade, {{at}}: the panel already had mailboxes on it.
mailNode.domainNotOnNode: The mail node no longer has this domain.
mailNode.unknownNote: The panel has no record of this domain: it was made on the node by hand. Adopt it to start its onboarding; mailboxes cannot be created on it until then.
mailNode.authoritativeNote: The tenant rejects unknown addresses of this domain itself (DBEB).
mailNode.markReadyNote: For a pilot or a test stand without a tenant.
mailNode.markReadyConfirm: Mailboxes can be created on {{domain}} right away, without the steps left. The change is journaled.
mailNode.errorDomainNotOnNode: The mail node has no such domain.
mailNode.errorDomainNotFound: The panel has no record of this domain: adopt it first.
mailNode.errorDomainKnown: The panel knows this domain already.
mailNode.errorStepOutOfOrder: Only the next step can be confirmed: reload the list.
mailNode.recreatedNote: The node reports another creation time for this domain ({{now}}) than the one the panel knows ({{was}}): the domain may have been deleted on the node and made again by hand, so its settings there may need applying again. Nothing changed in the panel: the domain keeps its state and takes mailboxes as before.
mailNode.acknowledgeNote: When the domain is set up on the node as it should be. If not, restart its onboarding instead.
mailNode.restartNote: Back to the first step. Mailboxes on the domain and their mail stay.
mailNode.restartConfirm: Start the onboarding of {{domain}} over? The confirmed steps and what the panel recorded about the domain on the node and in the tenant are cleared; the DKIM mode, the send limit and the values to publish you entered (expected MX, verification TXT, selector CNAMEs) stay. Mailboxes on the domain and their mail are not touched. Until the domain is ready again, no new mailbox can be created on it. The change is journaled.
mailNode.nodeUnreachableNote: The mail node could not be asked about this domain now: the panel's record is shown as it is and nothing in it changed.
mailNode.domainsNodeUnreachable: The mail node could not list its domains ({{reason}}). The domains below are the panel's record, unchanged; their state on the node is unknown until it answers again.
mailNode.recreatedBadge: Check: created again on the node?
mailNode.errorDomainNotRecreated: The node reports the creation time the panel knows already: nothing to accept.
mailNode.errorDomainNodeChanged: The node reports another creation time than the one shown: reload the list and check again.
mailNode.errorNothingToRestart: The domain is at the first step with nothing to clear.
mailNode.errorHostMismatch: This mailbox is on another mail host than the one in the mail node settings: nothing was changed.
mailNode.deleteAfterLabel: Days a mailbox keeps working after its deletion is asked for
mailNode.deleteAfterNote: From 1 to {{max}}. A change applies to deletions asked for from then on; dates already set stay.
mailNode.errorDeleteAfterDays: Enter a whole number of days from 1 to 90.
mailNode.errorPanelIps: Panel addresses must be up to 10 IP addresses or networks no wider than /24 (IPv4) or /48 (IPv6), such as 203.0.113.10 or 203.0.113.0/28.
mailNode.errorRateLimit: The send limit must be a whole number from 1 to 10000 messages.
mailNode.applyCodeEopHostMissing: the EOP host is not set
mailNode.applyCodeDkimDeleteUnconfirmed: the tenant signs, but mailcow still has a key: delete it below
mailNode.applyCodePrefilterDiffers: the spam filing rule is not on the node yet
mailNode.applyCodeDovecotRestartFailed: written, but Dovecot did not restart: it takes effect at its next start
mailNode.applyCounts: {{mailboxes}} on the node: {{matching}} in place, {{changed}} changed, {{failed}} failed; {{missing}} not on the node
mailNode.applyNote: What the panel sets on the node through the mailcow API: TLS and relayhost for the EOP host, the panel addresses in fail2ban, and for every domain its relayhost, DKIM key and the send limits of its mailboxes. Applying again changes only what differs.
mailNode.applyDone: Settings applied to the node: see the result.
mailNode.prefilterNote: The rule that files mail EOP marked as spam, bulk or phishing into Junk is not on the node yet. Whatever else the node's prefilter holds stays.
mailNode.prefilterConfirm: Writing the rule restarts Dovecot on the node: every IMAP session drops, the panel and mail apps reconnect within a minute. Apply now?
mailNode.prefilterDone: The spam filing rule is on the node.
mailNode.dkimDeleteNote: The tenant signs this domain's mail, but mailcow still has its DKIM key and signs with it too.
mailNode.dkimDeleteConfirm: Delete mailcow's DKIM key of {{domain}}? Mail of the domain goes out unsigned by the node from now on; a new key would need a new DNS record.
mailNode.rateLimitDiffers: (the panel sets {{limit}} at the next apply)
mailNode.rateLimitSaved: Send limit saved on the node.
mailNode.panelIpsNote: The addresses the panel reaches the node from, as the node sees them. The node's fail2ban never bans them, so a mailbox failing to sign in cannot cut the panel off. Up to 10, separated by commas.
mailNode.savedApplying: Saved. The node gets the panel's settings now; the result shows in the EOP section on the next load.
mailNode.applyCodePrefilterMarkersBroken: the node's prefilter has a MailExpert block without its end marker: fix it in mailcow, nothing was written
mailNode.applyCodePrefilterNotWritten: mailcow reported the rule written, but the node does not hold it
mailNode.applyCodeRelayhostInUse: kept: something else still sends through it
mailNode.applyItemPreviousTlsPolicy: TLS policy of the previous EOP host
mailNode.applyItemPreviousRelayhost: Relayhost of the previous EOP host
mailNode.errorExpectedMx: Expected MX must be up to 10 host names such as contoso-com.mail.protection.outlook.com.
mailNode.errorTenantTxt: The verification TXT must be printable text up to 255 characters without quotes, such as MS=ms12345678.
mailNode.errorDkimCname: A DKIM selector CNAME must be a host name.
mailNode.dnsCheckAll: Check DNS now: node and every domain
mailNode.dnsKeyFromLastApply: The node did not answer: compared with the key the last apply saw.
mailNode.dnsExpectedNote: What the domain must publish that the panel cannot read yet: until the panel works with the tenant, copy them from the Microsoft 365 admin center (the MX of the domain, the MS= verification record) and Get-DkimSigningConfig (Selector1CNAME, Selector2CNAME). Empty fields are not checked.
mailNode.dnsSummaryNode: DNS errors: the node, ready domains {{number}}
mailNode.nodeDnsNote: A and PTR of the node name and its address (EOP settings), no AAAA, and the certificate on port 587 after STARTTLS: end date, names, full chain. Checked every six hours; the results only warn and never change a domain.
mailNode.dnsCodeMxExpectedMissing: The expected MX is not entered yet, so it cannot be compared. DNS has: {{found}}. Enter the MX the tenant gives the domain under "Values to publish".
mailNode.dnsCodeMxMissing: The domain publishes no MX: mail to it cannot be delivered. Publish the record below.
mailNode.dnsCodeMxMismatch: The MX is not the one the tenant gives the domain: mail goes elsewhere, not through EOP. DNS has: {{found}}; must be: {{expected}}.
mailNode.dnsCodeMxExtra: Besides the expected MX the domain publishes others: some mail skips EOP. DNS has: {{found}}; must be only: {{expected}}.
mailNode.dnsCodeSpfMissing: The domain has no SPF record: receivers cannot tell mail from EOP is allowed. Publish the record below.
mailNode.dnsCodeSpfMultiple: The domain has more than one SPF record, and receivers then ignore all of them. Keep one: {{found}}.
mailNode.dnsCodeSpfNoInclude: The SPF record lacks include:spf.protection.outlook.com: mail sent through EOP fails SPF. DNS has: {{found}}.
mailNode.dnsCodeSpfNodeIp: SPF lists the node address: mail the node sends past EOP would still pass SPF. All mail leaves through EOP, so remove ip4 of the node.
mailNode.dnsCodeDkimKeyUnknown: The node has no DKIM key for the domain or could not be asked: apply the node settings, then check again.
mailNode.dnsCodeDkimMissing: The DKIM record is not published: the node signs mail with a key nobody can check. Publish the record below.
mailNode.dnsCodeDkimMismatch: The DKIM record carries another key than the one the node signs with: signatures fail. Replace it with the record below.
mailNode.dnsCodeDkimCnameExpectedMissing: The selector CNAMEs of EOP are not entered yet, so they cannot be compared. DNS has: {{found}}.
mailNode.dnsCodeDkimCnameMissing: A selector CNAME of EOP is not published: EOP cannot sign for the domain. Publish both records below.
mailNode.dnsCodeDkimCnameMismatch: A selector CNAME points elsewhere than Get-DkimSigningConfig says. DNS has: {{found}}; must be: {{expected}}.
mailNode.dnsCodeDmarcMissing: The domain has no DMARC record under {{name}}. Publish the record below (start with p=none).
mailNode.dnsCodeDmarcInvalid: The record under {{name}} does not start with v=DMARC1, so receivers ignore it. DNS has: {{found}}.
mailNode.dnsCodeDmarcMultiple: There is more than one DMARC record under {{name}}, and receivers then ignore them. Keep one: {{found}}.
mailNode.dnsCodeTenantTxtExpectedMissing: The tenant verification TXT is not entered yet, so it cannot be compared. MS= records in DNS: {{found}}.
mailNode.dnsCodeTenantTxtMissing: The tenant verification TXT is not published: the tenant cannot verify the domain. MS= records in DNS: {{found}}; must be: {{expected}}.
mailNode.dnsCodeMtaStsPublished: The domain publishes an MTA-STS policy ({{found}}). Its mx: lines must name the EOP MX, not the node: mailcow's own policy names the node, and senders that honour it would stop delivering. Check https://mta-sts.<domain>/.well-known/mta-sts.txt.
mailNode.dnsCodeLookupFailed: The lookup of {{name}} failed ({{detail}}): nothing could be compared. Check again later or check the resolver.
mailNode.dnsCodeResolverInvalid: DNS_CHECK_RESOLVER is not an IP address (with an optional port): no lookup was made.
mailNode.dnsCodeNodeIpMissing: The node address is not set (Mail node settings, next to the host), so A, PTR and SPF cannot be compared with it. DNS has: {{found}}.
mailNode.dnsCodeAMissing: The node name has no A record: nothing reaches the node by name. Publish the record below.
mailNode.dnsCodeAMismatch: The node name points elsewhere than the node address. DNS has: {{found}}; must be only: {{expected}}.
mailNode.dnsCodePtrMissing: The node address has no PTR record. Mail leaves through EOP, so nothing breaks, but ask the hosting provider to set it to the node name.
mailNode.dnsCodePtrMismatch: The PTR of the node address is not the node name. DNS has: {{found}}; must be: {{expected}}. Ask the hosting provider to change it.
mailNode.dnsCodeAaaaPresent: The node name has an AAAA record ({{found}}), but the node runs with IPv6 off: senders that try it first lose time before IPv4. Remove the AAAA.
mailNode.dnsCodeCertExpired: The certificate on port 587 has expired: EOP refuses the node's mail. Renew it on the node.
mailNode.dnsCodeCertExpiring: The certificate on port 587 ends in {{days}} days. Check that the node renews it.
mailNode.dnsCodeCertNameMismatch: The certificate does not carry {{missing}}: EOP checks the node by that name. Names on it: {{found}}.
mailNode.dnsCodeCertChainIncomplete: The node sends no chain from its certificate to a trusted root ({{detail}}): the intermediate certificate is missing, or the issuer is not a trusted CA. EOP then refuses the relay with 550 5.7.64 TenantAttribution. Install the full chain (fullchain.pem) on the node.
mailNode.dnsCodeCertUntrusted: The certificate chain does not reach a trusted root ({{detail}}): EOP refuses such a certificate. Use a certificate from a public CA.
mailNode.dnsCodeCertUnreachable: Port 587 of the node did not answer ({{detail}}): the certificate could not be read.
mailNode.dnsCodeStarttlsUnavailable: Port 587 of the node offers no STARTTLS: mail would go unencrypted.
mailNode.dnsCodeStarttlsRefused: Port 587 of the node refused STARTTLS: {{detail}}.
mailNode.dnsCodeCertHandshakeFailed: The TLS handshake on port 587 failed ({{detail}}).
mailNode.copyFailed: Could not copy: select the value and copy it
mailNode.dnsLookupFailedKept: The check of {{at}} could not ask DNS ({{reason}}). Shown below is the last check that could.
mailNode.dnsLookupFailedNone: The check of {{at}} could not ask DNS ({{reason}}), and no check has yet.
mailNode.dnsDmarcInherited: The domain has no DMARC record of its own: the one of {{domain}} covers it.
mailNode.dnsCodeSpfPassAll: SPF ends with +all: anyone may send mail as the domain and pass SPF. End it with -all or ~all.
mailNode.dnsCodeSpfNeutralAll: SPF ends with ?all: it says nothing about mail from anywhere else, so it protects nothing. End it with -all or ~all.
mailNode.dnsCodeCheckFailed: The check failed inside the panel ({{detail}}). Check again; if it repeats, look at the panel log.
mailNode.dnsVerdictLookupFailed: DNS check could not run last time; see the DNS block below
mailNode.dnsCheckStarted: The DNS check of the node and every domain runs in the background: reload the page in a minute to see the results.
mailNode.dnsCheckRunning: A DNS check of the node and every domain is already running: reload the page in a minute to see the results.
mailNode.nodeIpNote: The public address of the node. Only the DNS check uses it (A and PTR of the node name; SPF must not list it); the panel still connects by name. Change it together with the host when the node moves. Optional.

eop.title: Mail through EOP
eop.description: How mail of the node goes through Microsoft EOP. The next hop, its TLS, DKIM and the send limit are applied to the node when saved; the tenant fields are only kept for now.
eop.eopHostLabel: EOP host (next hop of the node)
eop.eopHostNote: The MX value of one of the tenant's domains, without brackets or port: the node sends every outgoing letter there.
eop.certificateHostNote: The name on the node's certificate: the tenant tells the node's mail apart by it. Usually the mail node host.
eop.dkimModeNote: mailcow signs until a tenant test shows that EOP signs mail relayed from the node.
eop.sendLimitLabel: Send limit of every mailbox without its own limit, messages per hour
eop.sendLimitNote: Stops a compromised mailbox before it blocks the shared connector. Up to {{max}}; an administrator changes it for one mailbox.
eop.terrlNote: The tenant's full limit of unique external recipients per 24 hours, from the EAC report. Leave empty to compute it from the licenses below. The ramp of a young tenant is applied on top: if the report already shows the ramped number, enter it here and leave the creation date empty.
eop.tenantNote: Kept for the tenant connection that comes later. The application certificate and its password never go into the panel.
eop.thumbprintNote: SHA-1, 40 hexadecimal characters; spaces and colons are dropped.
eop.checklistNote: Until the panel works with the tenant, each step is done by hand (see the runbook) and confirmed here with Done.
eop.errorEopHost: The EOP host must be a host name such as contoso-com.mail.protection.outlook.com.
eop.errorCertificateHost: The certificate host must be a host name such as mail.example.com.
eop.errorSendLimit: The send limit must be a whole number of messages per hour from 1 to 10000.
eop.errorTerrl: TERRL must be a whole number of recipients.
eop.errorAppId: The application ID is a GUID such as 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000.
eop.errorThumbprint: The thumbprint must be 40 hexadecimal characters.
eop.tlsPolicyNote: An entry in mailcow's TLS Policy Map for this exact host. secure for *.mail.protection.outlook.com; for a host under mx.microsoft the tenant test decides between secure, dane and no entry.
eop.tlsPolicySecure: secure: verified certificate, name of the host
eop.tlsPolicyDane: dane: DANE when the host publishes TLSA, else opportunistic TLS (cleartext possible)
eop.tlsPolicyVerify: verify: verified certificate, name from the parameters
eop.tlsPolicyEncrypt: encrypt: TLS required, certificate not checked (test stand)
eop.tlsPolicyDefault: No entry: mailcow's default (MTA-STS or DANE, else opportunistic TLS, cleartext possible)
eop.tlsParametersNote: Optional Postfix attributes, name=value separated by spaces, up to 255 characters. match= takes hostname, nexthop, dot-nexthop or host names for secure and verify, SHA-256 fingerprints (hex pairs) for fingerprint, where it is required, and is refused for the other policies. Changing the policy clears this field.
eop.errorTlsPolicy: Pick a TLS policy from the list.
eop.errorTlsParameters: Parameters must be name=value pairs up to 255 characters that fit the policy (see the hint).
eop.savedApplying: EOP settings saved. The node gets them now; the result shows here on the next load.
eop.errorNodeIp: The node address must be an IPv4 address such as 203.0.113.10.
eop.nodeIpReadOnlyNote: Set in "Mail node" next to the node host, so a move of the node changes both in one place.
eop.errorLicenses: Licenses must be a whole number from 1 to 1000000
eop.errorTenantCreated: Tenant creation date must be a date, not in the future
eop.budgetSettingsNote: Without a TERRL the limit is 500 × licenses^0.7 + 9500. A tenant younger than 31 days gets 10% of it, 31 to 60 days 25%, by the creation date. If the TERRL entered above is already the reduced limit of a young tenant (as the EAC report shows it), leave the creation date empty, or the reduction counts twice.
eop.budgetTitle: External recipients in the last 24 hours (TERRL budget)
eop.budgetUnavailable: The budget could not be read.
eop.budgetNoLimit: {{used}} unique external recipients; no limit set (enter TERRL or licenses).
eop.budgetWarn: At {{percent}}% or more: above the limit EOP stops all external mail of the tenant (550 5.7.233). The alert is raised too.
eop.budgetLogCovered: Counted from the panel journal and the node log, which covers the whole 24 hours.
eop.budgetLogPartial: Counted from the panel journal for 24 hours and the node log since {{at}}: forwards by rules and bounces before that are not counted.
eop.budgetLogUnread: The node log could not be read: counted from the panel journal only (no forwards by rules or bounces).

nodeOps.title: Node operations
nodeOps.description: Alerts about the mail node and EOP, and the node's mail queue. Every action is journaled.
nodeOps.alertsNote: Checked every five minutes: EOP refusals (5.7.711, 5.7.64, 5.7.233) and mail that went around EOP (needs the EOP host) in the last hour of the node log, the deferred queue, the certificate of the node, its containers and the TERRL budget.
nodeOps.sourceFailed: {{source}} could not be read: {{reason}}. Its alerts stay as they were.
nodeOps.pingNote: Optional, https. Every check pings it: success without alerts, /fail with them. A check that could not read the node sends nothing. Use a check of its own, not the disk one.
nodeOps.thresholdsNote: Either one raises the queue alert. Defaults: 20 messages, 60 minutes.
nodeOps.queueNote: Messages the node has not delivered yet. Deferred ones wait for the next try; held ones wait for an administrator. Deleting a message cannot be undone; the panel never deletes the whole queue.
nodeOps.flushed: The node is trying every deferred message again.
nodeOps.queueCounts: {{total}} in the queue: {{deferred}} deferred, {{hold}} held, {{active}} active
nodeOps.deleteConfirm: Delete message {{id}} from the queue? It will not be delivered.
nodeOps.bodyTruncated: Only the first 64 KB are shown.
nodeOps.alertConnectorBlocked: EOP blocked the inbound connector (5.7.711, AS(2204))
nodeOps.alertTenantAttribution: EOP refused the node: tenant attribution (5.7.64)
nodeOps.alertDetailQueue: {{deferred}} deferred, the oldest {{oldest}} min (thresholds: more than {{count}} or older than {{minutes}} min).
nodeOps.alertDetailTerrl: {{used}} of {{limit}} unique external recipients in 24 hours ({{percent}}%).
nodeOps.errorDeleteUnconfirmed: Deleting a queued message must be confirmed.
nodeOps.errorQueueItemNotFound: The message is no longer in the queue.
nodeOps.errorDeferredCount: The deferred message threshold must be a whole number from 1 to 100000.
nodeOps.errorDeferredMinutes: The deferred age threshold must be a whole number of minutes from 1 to 10080.
nodeOps.alertDetailEopHostMissing: Without it the panel cannot tell mail through EOP from mail around it, so the bypass check is off. Set it in the EOP section. This note does not fail the alert check.
nodeOps.errorQueueItemHeld: A held message is released first, then sent.
nodeOps.dumpTruncated: The message is larger than 2 MB: only its first 2 MB were read.
nodeOps.alertDetailRefusals_one: {{count}} refusal in the last hour, at {{at}}.
nodeOps.alertDetailRefusals_other: {{count}} refusals in the last hour, the last at {{at}}.
nodeOps.alertDetailBypass_one: {{count}} message sent through {{relays}} instead of EOP in the last hour, at {{at}}. Check the relayhost of the domains and extra.cf.
nodeOps.alertDetailBypass_other: {{count}} messages sent through {{relays}} instead of EOP in the last hour, the last at {{at}}. Check the relayhost of the domains and extra.cf.

quarantine.title: Mail node quarantine
quarantine.description: Letters the spam filter on the node (rspamd) refused or marked as spam: mailcow keeps a copy of each, and a refused letter exists only here. Open one to see why, read it as safe text, release it to its mailbox or delete it.
quarantine.descriptionUser: Letters to the panel's node mailboxes that the node's spam filter refused or marked as spam. Read-only: ask an administrator to release one.
quarantine.userView: Users see the entries of the panel's node mailboxes
quarantine.userViewNote: Read-only, under Settings > Mailboxes. Every user sees every node mailbox of this panel, so this shows them the quarantine of all of them. Releasing and deleting stay with administrators.
quarantine.settingsNote: Retention, maximum size and notifications live in mailcow (System > Configuration > Options > Quarantine); the mailcow API cannot read them back. A new mailcow keeps nothing until its maximum size and retention are above 0, and loses letters silently until that form was saved once. The panel can write them for you once: keep the release format "raw" there, the panel's texts about releasing assume it.
quarantine.filterPh: Filter by sender, recipient or subject
quarantine.historyUnread: The rspamd history could not be read, so the symbols are missing.
quarantine.emptyNote: Empty. If spam has come in, check that mailcow's quarantine keeps letters: a maximum size and a retention above 0.
quarantine.gone: This entry is no longer in the quarantine.
quarantine.safeNote: Shown as safe text: no images, no clickable links, and every link shows where it really goes. The letter's own HTML is never shown.
quarantine.truncated: The letter is long: only its beginning is shown.
quarantine.attachmentsLocked: Attachments of a quarantined letter cannot be opened from the panel.
quarantine.noteRejected: The node refused this letter, so it exists only here. Releasing hands it to the mailbox past the spam filter, removes the entry and teaches rspamd that it is not spam. The mailbox's own rules still apply.
quarantine.noteDelivered: This letter was already delivered to the mailbox's Spam folder; the quarantine holds a copy. Releasing teaches rspamd that it is not spam, but mailcow drops the released copy as a duplicate: move the letter out of Spam in the mailbox instead.
quarantine.noteOther: Releasing hands the letter to the mailbox past the spam filter, removes the entry and teaches rspamd that it is not spam.
quarantine.releaseEopNote: Microsoft EOP marked this letter too: the panel's filing rule puts it in Spam again, where it opens in safe view.
quarantine.deleteTitle: Delete this letter from the quarantine?
quarantine.deleteMessage: The copy from {{sender}} to {{rcpt}} is deleted from mailcow for good. A letter the node refused is then gone.
quarantine.nodeSettingsNever: The panel has not written mailcow's quarantine settings.
quarantine.nodeSettingsAppliedAt: The panel wrote mailcow's quarantine settings {{time}}.
quarantine.nodeSettingsWarning: This overwrites every quarantine setting in mailcow. The mailcow API cannot read them, so anything set there by hand is replaced, and the fields the panel leaves empty (notification sender, subject, template, BCC, redirect) go back to mailcow's defaults.
quarantine.nodeSettingsReapplyWarning: The panel wrote these settings before. Anything changed in mailcow since then (retention, size, notification template, sender, BCC, redirect, excluded domains) is overwritten again, with no way to read it first.
quarantine.nodeSettingsValues: Letters up to {{maxSize}} MiB, {{retention}} kept per mailbox, deleted after {{maxAge}} days, released as format "{{format}}", no excluded domains, notifications with mailcow's defaults.
quarantine.probablyOff: The quarantine is empty, but rspamd's recent history shows {{number}} letters to the panel's mailboxes that it refused or marked as spam. Unless they were released or deleted, mailcow's quarantine is probably off: enable it above.
quarantine.headersTruncated: Only the first headers are shown.
quarantine.releaseTraining: This cannot be undone: rspamd learns the letter as not spam and adds its fuzzy hash as ham, so similar letters score lower from now on.
quarantine.releaseRawNote: This assumes mailcow releases the original letter (release format "raw", which the panel sets).
quarantine.learnSpamTitle: Delete this letter and train rspamd with it as spam?
quarantine.learnSpamMessage: The copy from {{sender}} to {{rcpt}} is deleted from mailcow for good, and rspamd learns it as spam and adds its fuzzy hash, so similar letters score higher from now on. This cannot be undone.
